digest.component_or_area: plan review severity axes / impact model
propositions: The 'undecomposed' axis fires at 0.107% on plan-v3 (11/10,250 verified findings), two orders of magnitude below every other plan severity axis, and holds full hard-override power (any non-none grade floors impact at 0.85)

The axis's documented justification—that a deterministic G5 suppressor prevents false flat-plan findings on childless tickets—is factually incorrect: the veto fires zero times across 2,000 reviews and is inapplicable to 90%+ of the childless population

Of 29 total fires across both plan-v3 and plan-v4, the hard-override floor was the sole criterion driving impact in 25 cases, and 16 fires were graded 'low'—meaning the lowest-severity grade triggers the 0.85 floor, identical to miscalibrations already fixed in ac_unverifiable and divergent_implementation

The inverse population of findings text-matching the flat-plan regex but scored 'undecomposed'='none' is 33 (plan-v3) and 17 (plan-v4), but sampling shows these are false positives on code/module decomposition prose rather than missed plan-decomposition defects

The axis is neither working-as-intended (the suppressor is inert) nor completely unreachable (it fires stably on real tickets), but miscalibrated at the grade-to-floor mapping boundary, requiring a retune that gates the hard override on grade and removes the inert suppressor cite from axis text
